'''Justise Jon Winslow''' (born March 26, 1996) is an American professional [[basketball]] player who last played for the [[Wisconsin Herd]] of the [[NBA G League]]. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Duke Blue Devils]], with whom he won the [[2015 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament|2015 NCAA championship]].

==High school career==
Winslow was a four-year starter at [[St. John's School (Texas)|St. John's School]] in Houston, Texas. He started and ended his career at St. John's with league championships. He was the 2013 Gatorade Texas Player of the Year and averaged 27.5 points, 13.6 rebounds, 3.5 assists, 2.1 blocks, and 1.8 steals per game as a senior in 2013–14. Winslow was selected as a [[McDonald's All-American Game|McDonald's All-American]] in 2014.<ref name=PafMAAG>{{cite web|url=http://www.cbssports.com/collegebasketball/eye-on-college-basketball/24424133/players-announced-for-mcdonalds-all-american-game|title=Players announced for McDonald's All-American Game|access-date=November 20, 2014|date=January 1, 2013|author=Borzello, Jeff|work=[[CBS Sports]]}}</ref>

==College career==
Winslow averaged 14 points and five rebounds in his first five games in a Duke uniform. Duke coach [[Mike Krzyzewski]] compared Winslow's game to that of former Duke stars [[Tommy Amaker]] and [[Grant Hill]].<ref name=surprise>{{cite web|url=http://www.cbssports.com/collegebasketball/eye-on-college-basketball/24833646/surprisingly-its-justise-winslow-not-okafor-whos-been-dukes-best-frosh|title=Surprisingly, it's Justise Winslow, not Okafor, who's been Duke's best frosh|access-date=November 24, 2014|date=November 23, 2014|author=Norlander, Matt|work=[[CBS Sports]]}}</ref> On February 9, 2015, Winslow was named ACC Freshman of the Week,<ref name=ACCPOW11>{{cite web|title=ACC Basketball: Players of the Week Announced|url=http://www.theacc.com/news/acc-basketball-players-of-the-week-announced-02-09-2015|website=theACC.com|access-date=May 19, 2015|date=February 9, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150520153640/http://www.theacc.com/news/acc-basketball-players-of-the-week-announced-02-09-2015|archive-date=May 20, 2015|url-status=dead}}</ref> and later earned honorable mention All-ACC honors.<ref>{{cite web|title=ACSMA 2015 All-ACC Basketball Teams Announced|url=http://www.theacc.com/news/acsma-all-acc-basketball-teams-announced-03-08-2015|access-date=April 29, 2015|work=[[Atlantic Coast Conference]]|date=March 8, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150425010314/http://www.theacc.com/news/acsma-all-acc-basketball-teams-announced-03-08-2015|archive-date=April 25, 2015|url-status=dead}}</ref> In the NCAA tournament, Winslow averaged 14.3 points and 9.3 rebounds per game en route to a national championship. He played in 39 games for Duke as a freshman, averaging 12.6 points, 6.5 rebounds, 2.1 assists, and 1.3 steals in 29.1 minutes per game.<ref>{{cite web|title=Justise Winslow Stats|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/justise-winslow-1.html|work=Sports-Reference.com|access-date=February 28, 2016}}</ref>

In April 2015, Winslow declared for the [[NBA draft]], forgoing his final three years of collegiate eligibility.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Keeley|first1=Laure|title=Duke's Justise Winslow to enter NBA Draft|url=http://www.newsobserver.com/sports/college/acc/duke/article18521150.html|access-date=April 25, 2015|work=The News & Observer|date=April 14, 2015}}</ref>

Winslow started the Heat's first nine games of the 2016–17 season before missing the next 16 with a sore left wrist.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899819|title=Whiteside gets 26 points, 22 boards as Heat top Pacers 95-89|work=ESPN.com|date=December 14, 2016|access-date=December 15, 2016}}</ref> On December 22, 2016, he had a season-best game with 23 points and 13 rebounds in a 115–107 win over the [[Los Angeles Lakers]], as he set a career high for points and tied a career best in rebounds.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899881|title=Heat erase 19-point deficit, top Lakers 115-107|work=ESPN.com|date=December 22, 2016|access-date=December 22, 2016}}</ref> On January 5, 2017, Winslow was ruled out for the rest of the season after undergoing surgery to repair a torn labrum in his right shoulder.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/heat/news/justise-winslow-undergoes-right-shoulder-surgery|title=Justise Winslow Undergoes Right Shoulder Surgery|work=NBA.com|date=January 5, 2017|access-date=January 6, 2017}}</ref>

Winslow played in the first 27 games of the 2017–18 season<ref name=br1718>{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/w/winslju01/gamelog/2018/|title=Justise Winslow 2017-18 Game Log|work=basketball-reference.com|access-date=January 14, 2018}}</ref> but then missed 14 games with a knee strain.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975380|title=Heat beat Bucks 97-79, push winning streak to 7|work=ESPN.com|date=January 14, 2018|access-date=January 14, 2018}}</ref> On February 5, he scored 16 points against the [[Orlando Magic]].<ref name="br1718" /> He twice scored 17 points between February 24 and March 1, before setting a season-best 18 points on April 4 against the [[Atlanta Hawks]].<ref name="br1718" /> On March 12, he recorded 15 points and a season-high 13 rebounds against the [[Portland Trail Blazers]].<ref name="br1718" /> In Game 3 of the Heat's first-round playoff series against the [[Philadelphia 76ers]], Winslow scored a season-high 19 points in a 128–108 loss.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401029443|title=Embiid scores 23, 76ers top Heat 128-108 for 2-1 series lead|work=ESPN.com|date=April 19, 2018|access-date=April 19, 2018}}</ref>

On November 3, 2018, in his first start of the 2018–19 season, Winslow had 15 points, 10 rebounds and eight assists in a 123–118 loss to the [[Atlanta Hawks]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401070809|title=Trae Young scores 24 as Hawks beat Heat 123-118|work=ESPN.com|date=November 3, 2018|access-date=November 3, 2018}}</ref> On December 10, he scored a career-high 28 points with six 3-pointers in a 108–105 loss to the [[Los Angeles Lakers]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401071082|title=LeBron's Lakers edge Wade's Heat in final meeting, 108-105|work=ESPN.com|date=December 10, 2018|access-date=December 11, 2018}}</ref> After teammate and starting point guard [[Goran Dragić]] suffered a right knee injury, Winslow was named as Miami's starting point guard in mid-December.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/heats-justise-winslow-will-be-starting-point-guard/|title=Heat's Justise Winslow: Will be starting point guard|work=cbssports.com|date=December 26, 2018|access-date=December 28, 2018}}</ref> On December 28, he posted 24 points, 11 rebounds, and seven assists in a 118–94 win over the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401071197|title=Winslow, Adebayo lead Heat past Cavs, 118-94|work=ESPN.com|date=December 28, 2018|access-date=December 29, 2018}}</ref> On January 10, he recorded a career-high 11 assists in a 115–99 win over the [[Boston Celtics]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401071293|title=Wade scores 19, Heat hold off Celtics 115-99|work=ESPN.com|date=January 10, 2019|access-date=January 11, 2019}}</ref>

Winslow played in only 11 games for the Heat during the 2019–20 season as he was sidelined with a back injury.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.grizzlybearblues.com/platform/amp/2021/5/5/22420340/the-trials-of-justise-winslow-nba-memphis-grizzlies | title=The trials of Justise Winslow: The Rise, Deconstruction and hopeful rehab of Justise Winslow | publisher=SBNation | date=May 5, 2021 | access-date=October 22, 2022 | archive-date=October 22, 2022 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221022173312/https://www.grizzlybearblues.com/platform/amp/2021/5/5/22420340/the-trials-of-justise-winslow-nba-memphis-grizzlies | url-status=dead }}</ref>

===Memphis Grizzlies (2020–2021)===
On February 6, 2020, Winslow was acquired by the [[Memphis Grizzlies]] in a three-team trade also involving the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/memphis-grizzlies-acquire-justise-winslow-gorgui-dieng-and-dion-waiters-in-three-team-trade-with-miami-heat-and-minnesota-timberwolves-200206|title=Memphis Grizzlies acquire Justise Winslow, Gorgui Dieng and Dion Waiters in three-team trade with Miami Heat and Minnesota Timberwolves|work=NBA.com|date=February 6, 2020|access-date=February 6, 2020}}</ref> On July 21, the Grizzlies announced that Winslow had suffered a [[hip]] injury during team practice and would miss the rest of the 2019–20 season.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/justise-winslow-medical-update-200721|title=Justise Winslow medical update|date=July 21, 2020|website=NBA.com|access-date=July 21, 2020}}</ref>

===Los Angeles Clippers (2021–2022)===
On August 8, 2021, Winslow signed a two-year contract with the [[Los Angeles Clippers]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/clippers/news/la-clippers-sign-justise-winslow|title=LA Clippers Sign Justise Winslow|work=NBA.com|date=August 8, 2021}}</ref>

===Portland Trail Blazers (2022–2023)===
On February 4, 2022, Winslow was traded, alongside [[Eric Bledsoe]], [[Keon Johnson (basketball, born 2002)|Keon Johnson]], and a 2025 second-round pick, to the [[Portland Trail Blazers]] in exchange for [[Norman Powell]] and [[Robert Covington]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.oregonlive.com/blazers/2022/02/portland-trail-blazers-trade-norman-powell-robert-covington-to-la-clippers-for-eric-bledsoe-justise-winslow-keon-johnson-report.html?outputType=amp|title = Portland Trail Blazers trade Norman Powell, Robert Covington to LA Clippers for Eric Bledsoe, Justise Winslow, Keon Johnson|date = February 4, 2022}}</ref>

On December 21, 2022, during a 101–98 loss to the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]], Winslow exited the game with a left ankle injury. On December 26, the Trail Blazers announced that he had been diagnosed with a Grade 2 ankle sprain and would be re-evaluated in two weeks.<ref>{{Cite web |date=December 26, 2022 |title=Justise Winslow Injury Update |url=https://www.nba.com/blazers/news/justise-winslow-injury-update |access-date=March 17, 2023 |website=NBA}}</ref> After the All-Star break, Winslow received a second opinion on his injury and underwent a bone marrow aspirate concentrate procedure in March to address further discomfort in his left ankle.<ref>{{Cite web |date=March 17, 2023 |title=Trail Blazers Medical Update |url=https://www.nba.com/blazers/news/trail-blazers-medical-update-2 |access-date=March 17, 2023 |website=NBA}}</ref> On March 29, he underwent season-ending left ankle surgery.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Justise Winslow Medical Update |url=https://www.nba.com/blazers/news/justise-winslow-medical-update |access-date=March 29, 2023 |website=NBA}}</ref>

===Raptors 905 (2023–2024)===
On October 20, 2023, Winslow signed with the [[Toronto Raptors]],<ref>{{cite web|first=Sam|last=Amico|title=Raptors Sign Justise Winslow, Waive Makur Maker|url=https://hoopswire.com/raptors-sign-justise-winslow-waive-makur-maker/|website=HoopsWire.com|date=October 20, 2023|access-date=October 22, 2023}}</ref> but was waived the same day.<ref>{{cite web|title=RAPTORS WAIVE DOWTIN JR, GUEYE AND WINSLOW|url=https://www.nba.com/raptors/news/raptors-waive-dowtin-jr-gueye-and-winslow|website=NBA.com|date=October 20, 2023|access-date=October 22, 2023}}</ref> On October 30, 2023, Winslow joined [[Raptors 905]].<ref>{{cite web|title=RAPTORS 905 FINALIZES TRAINING CAMP ROSTER|url=https://raptors905.gleague.nba.com/news/raptors-905-finalizes-training-camp-roster-2|website=NBA.com|date=October 30, 2023|access-date=December 11, 2023}}</ref>

On February 10, 2024, Winslow signed a 10-day contract with Toronto,<ref>{{cite web|title=RAPTORS SIGN WINSLOW AND GUEYE TO 10-DAY CONTRACTS|url=https://www.nba.com/raptors/news/raptors-sign-winslow-and-gueye-to-10-day-contracts|website=NBA.com|date=February 10, 2024|access-date=February 10, 2024}}</ref> but didn't play for them. On February 20, he returned to Raptors 905.<ref>{{cite web|title=2023-2024 Raptors 905 Transaction History|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/gleague/teams/Raptors-905/41/Transaction_History/2024|website=RealGM.com|access-date=February 21, 2024}}</ref>

===Wisconsin Herd (2024–2025)===
On October 16, 2024, Winslow signed with the [[Milwaukee Bucks]], but was waived the next day.<ref>{{cite web|first=Rory|last=Maher|title=Bucks Sign, Waive Justise Winslow|url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2024/10/bucks-to-sign-justise-winslow-to-exhibit-10-deal.html|website=HoopsRumors.com|date=October 17, 2024|access-date=October 19, 2024}}</ref> On October 28, he joined the [[Wisconsin Herd]].<ref>{{cite web|title=WISCONSIN HERD ANNOUNCES 2024-25 TRAINING CAMP ROSTER|url=https://wisconsin.gleague.nba.com/news/wisconsin-herd-announces-2024-25-training-camp-roster|website=NBA.com|date=October 28, 2024|access-date=October 29, 2024}}</ref>

==National team career==
In 2012, Winslow played for the United States at the [[2012 FIBA Under-17 World Championship|FIBA Under-17 World Championship]], where he was named to the [[FIBA Under-17 Basketball World Cup All-Tournament Team|All-Tournament Team]]. In 2013, he played at the [[2013 FIBA Under-19 World Championship|FIBA Under-19 World Championship]]. In 2014, he played at the [[2014 FIBA Americas Under-18 Championship|FIBA Americas Under-18 Championship]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://archive.fiba.com/pages/eng/fa/player/p/pid/99011/sid/6228/tid/379/_/2012_FIBA_U17_World_Championship_for_Men/index.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130403135125/http://archive.fiba.com/pages/eng/fa/player/p/pid/99011/sid/6228/tid/379/_/2012_FIBA_U17_World_Championship_for_Men/index.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=April 3, 2013|title=Justise Winslow's profile|work=FIBA.com|access-date=September 3, 2018}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Winslow is the son of Robin Davis and [[Rickie Winslow]]. His father played basketball for the [[Houston Cougars men's basketball|University of Houston]] from 1983 to 1987, where he was a member of the famed [[Phi Slama Jama]] team that included [[Hakeem Olajuwon]] and [[Clyde Drexler]], and was selected 28th overall by the [[Chicago Bulls]] in the [[1987 NBA draft]]. Winslow has three older brothers, Cedrick, Brandon and Josh; and an older sister, Bianca. His brother, Josh, played football at [[Dartmouth Big Green football|Dartmouth]], while his sister, Bianca, was a basketball player at [[Houston Cougars women's basketball|Houston]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.goduke.com/ViewArticle.dbml?ATCLID=209693412|title=Justise Winslow Bio|work=GoDuke.com|access-date=February 28, 2016|archive-date=June 21, 2015|archive-url=https://archive.today/20150621163314/http://www.goduke.com/ViewArticle.dbml?ATCLID=209693412|url-status=dead}}</ref>
